testimony:
Action-by-action appraisal (≤180 words)

A1 – Send generator to Neonatal ICU  
• Least-advantaged affected group: the eight premature infants facing near-certain death without power.  
• Comparative position: survives and retains the primary good of life; no other group becomes worse-off than “immediate fatality.”  
• Relevant primary good / liberty: life and bodily integrity (fundamental for exercising any liberty).  

A0 – Send generator to Water-Treatment Plant  
• Least-advantaged affected group: the same eight infants, now left to die. (Residents who might suffer later sanitation illnesses are at risk but not yet at the brink of certain death.)  
• Comparative position: falls from survival to imminent death—an extreme loss of basic primary goods.  
• Relevant primary good / liberty: life and bodily integrity forfeited for these infants.  

Rawlsian comparison  
The difference principle requires arranging institutions so that the worst-off class is as well off as possible. Under both actions, the infants remain the worst-off, but A1 markedly improves (indeed saves) their lives, whereas A0 extinguishes them. Safeguarding tens of thousands from a probabilistic health threat does not justify sacrificing an identifiable group’s inviolable life interest (E2). Numerical magnitude is therefore SECONDARY: it cannot override protection of the least-advantaged when basic survival is at stake.

Rawlsian Recommendation: Favor A1.
[/INST]
